name: Tanhumet
title: Father of Seraiah from Netophah
summary: Tanhumet was a Netophathite and the father of Seraiah, one of the military leaders who came to Gedaliah, the governor of Judah, after the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC. He is a lesser-known biblical figure mentioned in connection with the remnant group that remained in Judah after the Babylonian conquest.

keyEvents.title: Seraiah's arrival at Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Tanhumet's son Seraiah was among the commanders who came to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, in Mizpah after the destruction of Jerusalem to submit to Babylonian rule.

keyEvents.title: Gedaliah swears loyalty
keyEvents.description: Gedaliah swore to Seraiah, Tanhumet's son, and the other officers that they need not fear the Chaldeans, and urged them to settle in the land.

keyEvents.title: Warning about Ishmael's conspiracy
keyEvents.description: Johanan and the other commanders, including those around Tanhumet's son Seraiah, warned Gedaliah that Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, planned to kill him.

keyEvents.title: The Murder of Gedaliah
keyEvents.description: Despite the warnings, Gedaliah was killed by Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, which had dramatic consequences for the remaining group in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Flight to Egypt
keyEvents.description: After the murder of Gedaliah, Serajah, son of Tahpenes, and the other commanders feared Babylonian revenge and took the people with them to Egypt against the prophet Jeremiah's advice.
